nodes.summary: For real numbers $a$, $b$ and $D$ with $|a - b| \le D$, the integers $\lfloor a \rfloor$ and $\lfloor b \rfloor$ satisfy $|\lfloor a \rfloor - \lfloor b \rfloor| \le \lceil D \rceil$.
nodes.title: Floor differences are bounded by a ceiling

nodes.summary: Let $d$ and $n$ be natural numbers, let $K \ge 0$, and let $f$ be a $K$-Lipschitz map from the unit cube $[0, 1]^d$ to $\mathbb{R}^n$, both carrying the sup distance. For every real $t \ge 1$, the cardinality of the integer cube set of $f$ at scale $t$, taken as a natural number, is at most $\lceil t \rceil^d \, (2 \lceil K \sqrt{d} \rceil + 3)^n$.
nodes.title: Counting integer cubes met by a dilated Lipschitz image

nodes.summary: Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, let $f_1, \dots, f_m : [0,1]^d \to \mathbb{R}^n$ be maps whose ranges together cover the frontier of $S$, and let $t$ be a real number. Let $O$ and $I$ be the outer and inner cube sets of $S$ at scale $t$: the $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ for which some, respectively every, point $x$ of the half-open unit cube $\prod_i [v_i, v_i + 1)$ has $x / t \in S$ (coordinatewise, with $x / 0 = 0$). Let…
nodes.title: Counting outer cubes by inner cubes and boundary charts

nodes.summary: Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ and $t > 0$. The number of integer vectors $x \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ with $x / t \in S$ equals the lattice enumerator of $S$ at $t$, the number of points of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ in the dilate $tS$; here an infinite set is counted as $0$.
nodes.title: Integer count of a dilate

nodes.summary: Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be bounded, let $t > 0$, and let $\mathrm{vol}(S)$ be the Lebesgue (outer) measure of $S$, which is finite. For $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ let $Q_v = \prod_i [v_i, v_i + 1)$. Let $I$ be the inner cube set of $S$ at scale $t$, the $v$ with $Q_v \subseteq tS$, and $O$ the outer cube set, the $v$ with $Q_v$ meeting $tS$. Then $|I| \le \mathrm{vol}(S)\, t^n \le |O|$.
nodes.title: Cubical measure sandwich

nodes.summary: Let $d$ and $n$ be natural numbers, let $K \ge 0$, and let $f$ be a $K$-Lipschitz map from the unit cube $[0, 1]^d$ to $\mathbb{R}^n$, both carrying the sup distance. Then there is a real number $C > 0$ such that for every real $t \ge 1$, the cardinality of the integer cube set of $f$ at scale $t$, taken as a natural number, is at most $C t^d$.
nodes.title: Dilated Lipschitz images meet $O(t^d)$ integer cubes

nodes.summary: Let $d$ and $n$ be natural numbers, let $K \ge 0$, and let $f$ be a $K$-Lipschitz map from the unit cube $[0, 1]^d$ to $\mathbb{R}^n$, both carrying the sup distance. For every real $t \ge 1$, the integer cube set of $f$ at scale $t$ is finite.
nodes.title: Dilated Lipschitz images meet finitely many integer cubes

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a bounded set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and a real number $t > 0$, the set $(tP) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ of points of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the dilate $tP = \{tp : p \in P\}$ is finite.
nodes.title: Finiteness of the lattice points in a positive dilate

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a bounded set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and any real number $t$, the set $(tP) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ of points of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the dilate $tP = \{tp : p \in P\}$ is finite.
nodes.title: Finiteness of the lattice points in a dilate

nodes.summary: If $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is bounded and $t > 0$, then the outer cube set of $S$ at scale $t$, the set of $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ whose integer unit cube $\prod_i [v_i, v_i + 1)$ meets $tS$, is finite.
nodes.title: Finiteness of the outer cube set

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a bounded set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, a real number $t > 0$ and a vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, the set $(tP + x) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ of points of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the translated dilate $tP + x = \{tp + x : p \in P\}$ is finite.
nodes.title: Finiteness of the lattice points in a translated positive dilate

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a bounded set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, any real number $t$ and a vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, the set $(tP + x) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ of points of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the translated dilate $tP + x = \{tp + x : p \in P\}$ is finite.
nodes.title: Finiteness of the lattice points in a translated dilate

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be metric spaces, let $d$ be a natural number and let $f : X \to Y$ be a Lipschitz map. If a set $B \subseteq X$ is $d$-Lipschitz parametrizable, then its image $f(B) \subseteq Y$ is $d$-Lipschitz parametrizable.
nodes.title: Lipschitz images of Lipschitz parametrizable sets

nodes.summary: For every set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ and every real $t$, the inner cube set of $S$ at scale $t$ is contained in the outer cube set of $S$ at scale $t$.
nodes.title: Inner cube indices are outer cube indices

nodes.summary: For a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ and a real number $t$, the inner cube set of $S$ at scale $t$ is the set of $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ such that $(x_1/t, \dots, x_n/t) \in S$ for every $x$ in the integer unit cube $Q_v = \prod_i [v_i, v_i + 1)$. For $t > 0$ these are the $v$ with $Q_v \subseteq tS$; for $t = 0$ the division is read as $x_i/0 = 0$.
nodes.title: Inner cube set

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a map from the unit cube $[0, 1]^d$ to $\mathbb{R}^n$ and let $t$ be a real number. The integer cube set of $f$ at scale $t$ is the set of integer vectors $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ for which some point $y$ of the unit cube satisfies $v_i \le t f(y)_i < v_i + 1$ for every coordinate $i$, that is, the set of integer vectors whose half-open unit cube $\prod_i [v_i, v_i + 1)$ meets the dilate $t \cdot f([0, 1]^d)$.
nodes.title: Integer cube set

nodes.summary: For $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, the integer unit cube at $v$ is the half-open cube $Q_v = \prod_i [v_i, v_i + 1) \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, the set of $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with $v_i \le x_i < v_i + 1$ for every coordinate $i$.
nodes.title: Integer unit cube

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a metric space. Every finite set $B \subseteq X$ is $d$-Lipschitz parametrizable for every natural number $d$.
nodes.title: Finite sets are Lipschitz parametrizable

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a metric space and $d$ a natural number. Every finite set $s$ of points of $X$, given as a finset, is $d$-Lipschitz parametrizable.
nodes.title: Finsets are Lipschitz parametrizable

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a metric space. For every natural number $d$, the empty subset of $X$ is $d$-Lipschitz parametrizable, via the empty family of maps.
nodes.title: The empty set is Lipschitz parametrizable

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a metric space. For every natural number $d$ and every point $x \in X$, the set $\lbrace x \rbrace$ is $d$-Lipschitz parametrizable, via a single constant map.
nodes.title: Singletons are Lipschitz parametrizable

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a metric space and $d$ a natural number. A set $B \subseteq X$ is $d$-Lipschitz parametrizable if there are a natural number $n$ (possibly $0$) and Lipschitz maps $f_1, \dots, f_n : [0, 1]^d \to X$ out of the closed unit cube $[0, 1]^d \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ such that $B$ equals the union of their images, $B = f_1([0, 1]^d) \cup \dots \cup f_n([0, 1]^d)$.
nodes.title: Lipschitz parametrizable sets

nodes.summary: For every natural number $d$ and every real number $t$, the lattice-point count of the empty set $\emptyset \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ at the dilate $t$ is $0$.
nodes.title: The lattice-point count of the empty set vanishes

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a bounded set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and a real number $t > 0$, the lattice-point enumerator $L_P(t)$ is the number of points of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the dilate $tP = \{tp : p \in P\}$, that is, $L_P(t) = |(tP) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d|$.
nodes.title: Lattice-point enumerator

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and a real number $t$, this is the number of elements of the set $(tP) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ of points of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the dilate $tP = \{tp : p \in P\}$, where an infinite set is assigned the value $0$.
nodes.title: Lattice-point count of a real dilate

nodes.summary: Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be bounded, and suppose its boundary $\partial S$ is $(n-1)$-Lipschitz parametrizable: it is the union of the ranges of finitely many Lipschitz maps from the unit cube $[0,1]^{n-1}$, where $n - 1$ is read as $0$ when $n = 0$. Then there is a real constant $C$ such that for all sufficiently large real $t$, the lattice enumerator $L_S(t)$, the number of points of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ in $tS$,…
nodes.title: Lattice-point count of a dilate with boundary error

nodes.summary: Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be bounded, let $f_1, \dots, f_m$ be maps from the unit cube $[0,1]^d$ to $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose ranges cover the boundary $\partial S$, and let $t > 0$. For each $i$, let $N_i(t)$ be the number of $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ such that $t f_i(y)$ lies in the half-open cube $\prod_j [v_j, v_j + 1)$ for some $y \in [0,1]^d$, and assume each of these sets of $v$ is finite. Then the lattice…
nodes.title: Lattice-point error bound from boundary charts

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and a real number $t > 0$, this is the set $(tP) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ of points of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the dilate $tP = \{tp : p \in P\}$.
nodes.title: Lattice points in a positive dilate

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and a real number $t$, this is the set $(tP) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ of points of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the dilate $tP = \{tp : p \in P\}$.
nodes.title: Lattice points in a dilate

nodes.summary: For $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, $t \in \mathbb{R}$ and $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, $v$ belongs to the inner cube set of $S$ at scale $t$ if and only if $(x_1/t, \dots, x_n/t) \in S$ for every $x$ in the integer unit cube at $v$.
nodes.title: Membership in the inner cube set

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a map from the unit cube $[0, 1]^d$ to $\mathbb{R}^n$, let $t$ be a real number and let $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$. Then $v$ belongs to the integer cube set of $f$ at scale $t$ if and only if some point $y$ of the unit cube satisfies $v_i \le t f(y)_i < v_i + 1$ for every coordinate $i$.
nodes.title: Membership in the integer cube set

nodes.summary: For $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, $x$ lies in the integer unit cube at $v$ if and only if $v_i \le x_i < v_i + 1$ for every coordinate $i$.
nodes.title: Membership in an integer unit cube

nodes.summary: For $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, $t \in \mathbb{R}$ and $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, $v$ belongs to the outer cube set of $S$ at scale $t$ if and only if $(x_1/t, \dots, x_n/t) \in S$ for some $x$ in the integer unit cube at $v$.
nodes.title: Membership in the outer cube set

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ lies in the standard lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the integer span of the standard basis vectors of $\mathbb{R}^d$, exactly when every coordinate $x_i$ of $x$ is an integer.
nodes.title: Membership in the standard lattice

nodes.summary: For a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ and a real number $t$, the outer cube set of $S$ at scale $t$ is the set of $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ such that $(x_1/t, \dots, x_n/t) \in S$ for some $x$ in the integer unit cube $Q_v = \prod_i [v_i, v_i + 1)$. For $t > 0$ these are the $v$ with $Q_v$ meeting $tS$; for $t = 0$ the division is read as $x_i/0 = 0$.
nodes.title: Outer cube set

nodes.summary: Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, let $f_1, \dots, f_m : [0,1]^d \to \mathbb{R}^n$ be maps whose ranges together cover the frontier of $S$, and let $t$ be a real number. For $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ write $Q_v$ for the half-open unit cube $\prod_i [v_i, v_i + 1)$. If $v$ lies in the outer cube set of $S$ at scale $t$ (some $x \in Q_v$ has $x / t \in S$, coordinatewise, with $x / 0 = 0$) but not in the inner cube set (not…
nodes.title: Boundary cubes meet the dilated frontier charts

nodes.summary: Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ and $t > 0$. Viewing an integer vector as a real vector gives a bijection from the set of $x \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ with $x / t \in S$ onto the lattice point set $tS \cap \mathbb{Z}^n$.
nodes.title: Integer points of a dilate

nodes.summary: Let $K \ge 0$, let $f$ be a $K$-Lipschitz map from the unit cube $[0, 1]^d$ to $\mathbb{R}^n$, both carrying the sup distance, and let $t$ and $T$ be real numbers with $0 < t \le T$. If $y$ and $y'$ are points of the unit cube at distance at most $1/T$, then $|t f(y)_i - t f(y')_i| \le K$ for every coordinate $i$.
nodes.title: Dilated Lipschitz maps vary by at most $K$ on cells of size $1/T$

nodes.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, the standard integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is the $\mathbb{Z}$-submodule of $\mathbb{R}^d$ (the real-valued functions on $\{0, \dots, d-1\}$) spanned by the standard basis vectors $e_0, \dots, e_{d-1}$.
nodes.title: The standard integer lattice

nodes.summary: For every $d \in \mathbb{N}$, every real $t$ and every $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, the translated lattice-point count $|((t \cdot \emptyset) + x) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d|$ is $0$.
nodes.title: The translated lattice-point count of the empty set is zero

nodes.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$, let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded set, let $t > 0$ be real and let $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$. The translated lattice-point enumerator is $F_{t,P}(x) = |((t \cdot P) + x) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d|$, the number of points of the standard integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the dilate $t \cdot P$ translated by $x$.
nodes.title: Translated lattice-point enumerator of a bounded set

nodes.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, a real $t$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, the translated lattice-point count is the number of elements of the translated lattice-point set $((t \cdot P) + x) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$, taken to be $0$ when this set is infinite.
nodes.title: Translated lattice-point count for arbitrary sets

nodes.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, a real $t > 0$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, this is the set $((t \cdot P) + x) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ of points of the standard integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the dilate $t \cdot P$ translated by $x$. No boundedness of $P$ is assumed.
nodes.title: Translated lattice-point set at a positive dilation

nodes.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, a real $t$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, the translated lattice-point set is $((t \cdot P) + x) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$, the set of points of the standard integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the dilate $t \cdot P$ translated by $x$.
nodes.title: Translated lattice-point set

nodes.summary: For every natural number $d$, the origin of $\mathbb{R}^d$ lies in the closed unit cube $[0, 1]^d$.
nodes.title: The origin lies in the unit cube

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, the closed unit cube $[0, 1]^d$ is the set of points $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with $0 \le x_i \le 1$ for every coordinate $i$.
nodes.title: The unit cube

nodes.summary: For every $d \in \mathbb{N}$, the origin of $\mathbb{R}^d$ lies in the standard integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$.
nodes.title: The origin is a lattice point

conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.
